summary: Follow-up acceptance of 0eb0b4b against prior reviews of eb28866. All three prior MAJORs are closed: (E1) check_kinds derives suites from the declared category plus actual changed file classes using trusted base masks; run_checks runs every applicable suite on the exact tip; full_green/verification enforce recorded suite coverage via checks_cover (legacy records without 'suites' fail closed and force a rerun); apply_partial refuses multi-suite selection; unit_has_checks/waiver_valid now consider all touched classes, so a waiver cannot hide a configured other-class suite; the stale-known-checks cache in _do_review is still caught by ensure_full/cmd_integrate gates. Regression test demonstrates backend-unit/frontend-change coverage, stale single-suite rejection and waiver blocking. (E2) _do_review requires LEAD == u['author'] for non-candidate units before any model call and before cached-verdict reuse, so a switched lead cannot self-review nor launder a cached PASS into 'accepted'; regression proves zero paid calls on the blocked path and finish from the other chat afterwards. (E3) Per the stated ground truth the space before the at-sign is a payload rendering artifact absent from the exact git bytes; the new simulated npm-global .cmd-shim discovery test passes and no space was introduced. Prior MINORs E4–E6 and T1–T5 are all addressed: author line prints the actual service/model, shared author/cycle recovery guidance, profile explicitly rejects inert flags, JSONL split strictly on LF with Unicode-separator regression, controlled Blocked for invalid JSON and nested message/content/model shapes, installer reparse detection via lstat st_file_attributes (works on Python 3.9–3.11, test included), credential edit-denies mirrored, AGENTS.md rules path corrected. The next_step fix correctly stops reusing accepted() (which requires completed integration) and suggests integrate only on matching PASS plus verification; matrix test asserts it. Manifest/docs updated consistently; benchmark worktree isolation is benign. No new BLOCKER/MAJOR found. Three new MINOR issues are reported together below; none accepts unverified code — the coverage-adjacent ones either depend on overlapping trusted masks or fail closed with poor recovery guidance.

findings.problem: check_kinds breaks after the first matching category per file. If the trusted base masks for frontend and backend overlap (e.g. a JS fullstack repo with '*.js' in both class masks, or frontend '*.js' plus backend 'server/*.js'), a file matching both is counted only as frontend and the configured backend suite is never added for it.
findings.scenario: Trusted config: checks.frontend and checks.backend both configured; frontend masks include '*.js', backend masks include 'server/*.js'. A frontend-kind unit changes server/api.js. check_kinds matches frontend first and breaks, so kinds={'frontend'}; only the frontend suite runs, checks_cover sees required={'frontend'} and passes, and integrate/finish report VERIFIED although the configured backend suite applicable to that file never ran — a narrow residual of the E1 failure mode, conditional on overlapping masks (default masks are presumably disjoint, hence MINOR not MAJOR).
findings.fix: Remove the break and add every matching category for each changed file (kinds.add per match, no break). This is a one-line change, cannot reduce coverage, and makes suite selection independent of mask ordering/overlap. Add a regression with overlapping masks asserting both suites are required.

findings.problem: For a mixed-class change where one touched class has NO configured suite, run_checks aggregates configured=all(...) to False and store_full blocks, while waiver_valid is simultaneously False because unit_has_checks sees the other class's configured suite. The unconfigured suite's blocker guidance (waive) can therefore never succeed: the task is deadlocked with misleading recovery advice.
findings.scenario: Repo configures only checks.backend (Python backend + static frontend, a common layout). A backend unit also touches a small .tsx file. check_kinds returns ['backend','frontend']; the frontend suite is unconfigured, so the aggregated result is configured=False with a blocker suggesting waive; CR waive is rejected because checks.backend is configured. The lead follows the printed guidance in circles; the only real exits (configure checks.frontend in the base via a separate task, or split the unit) are not stated. Behavior is fail-closed and the prior fix explicitly sanctioned rejecting uncovered mixed-class commits, so this is a guidance/recovery defect, not an acceptance hole.
findings.fix: Detect the 'touched class without configured checks' case explicitly and emit a dedicated blocker naming the class and the two real recoveries (add the suite to the trusted base config in a separate task, or split the unit), instead of the generic per-suite unconfigured/waive message; alternatively treat only configured suites as required and document that unconfigured touched classes are covered by the waiver reason — but do not leave waive suggested while structurally impossible.

findings.problem: linked() gates the Windows reparse-point check behind path.exists(), which follows the link. A dangling junction/symlink-to-missing-target (is_symlink() False for junctions, exists() False because the target is gone) returns False and bypasses the guard; lstat would still see the reparse attribute. The exists() guard is only needed to avoid FileNotFoundError on not-yet-created parents.
findings.scenario: Windows, pre-existing junction ~/.agents/skills/agentq -> ~/.claude/skills/agentq whose target directory was deleted (paused Claude cleanup). linked() reports False for every parent, so the 'linked installation path' refusal is skipped; if the junction target is (re)created before or during --apply (another process, or the operator restoring Claude files), the installer backs up and writes through the junction into the Claude tree, violating the preservation guarantee. Impact is narrow because writes through a truly dangling junction normally fail and out-of-home targets are still caught by resolve()+relative_to, hence MINOR.
findings.fix: Replace the exists() gate with a direct lstat: try attrs = path.lstat() except (FileNotFoundError, OSError): return False; then test st_file_attributes & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT on nt. This detects dangling reparse points and keeps missing parents harmless; extend the reparse regression with a dangling-junction case (exists()=False, lstat succeeds with 0x400).
